last_attempts_log.asr_text: Every morning, the employee looks for an empty desk. Someone else may have used it yesterday, and someone new may sit there tomorrow. They cannot leave papers in a drawer, and they sometimes worry about using a desk or keyboard after someone else. Before work begins, they have already spent time finding a place. They miss the same desk, drawer, and view. They helped them start without searching and gave them a quiet sense of belonging. Now the office can feel borrowed. They want their work and things to have a place, even when they cannot choose the seating policy.

last_attempts_log.asr_text: Some mornings, the employee chooses a quiet corner because they need to think. On other days, they sit where conversation is easy. A different desk can bring them closer to people from another department. It can also give them distance when a workplace relationship feels uncomfortable, or when they simply need room. Since working from home gave them a place of their own, they don’t need one fixed spot at the office. They value being able to change their surroundings and choose a place that fits their mood, their task, and the people they need or do not need around them.
